content: PRIMA1, also referred to as Proline-rich membrane anchor 1, is a protein encoded by the PRIMA1 gene in humans. PRiMA is responsible for organizing acetylcholinesterase (AChE) into tetramers and anchoring AChE to the membranes of neural cells. This function is mediated by the proline-rich anchor domain (PRAD) of PRIMA1, which secures the AChE tetramer to the plasma membrane of neural cells and myocytes. The PRAD specifically interacts with the C-terminal T-peptide of AChE. PRiMA plays a critical role in targeting AChE to the cell surface. In neuroblastoma cells, PRiMA is the limiting factor for this targeting process. Both humans and mice express PRiMA in two alternative splice variants, which differ in their cytoplasmic regions. The clinical significance of PRiMA lies in its association with neurodegenerative diseases. The degradation of AChE has been linked to the severity of conditions such as Alzheimer’s disease.
